exposure: Second twins born by caesarean section (C-section) after a vaginally delivered first twin
caesarean section (C-section) after a vaginally delivered first twin
cohort: 2111 liveborn very low-birthweight (VLBW) twin infants, with gestational age (GA) from 23(+0) weeks to 31(+6) weeks, without congenital anomalies, admitted to the collaborating centres of the Spanish SEN1500 neonatal network from 2011 to 2020
finding: In this study of very low birth weight twins, second twins had a higher risk of RDS, but no other differences in morbidity or mortality were found except for second twins delivered by C-section after a first twin delivered vaginally, who had decreased overall survival and survival without major brain injury.
mod_finding: Second twins born by caesarean section (C-section) after a vaginally delivered first twin had less overall survival and survival without MBD.
